title: Turn two compounding lessons into tests instead of prose
action: A compounding triage found two lessons from opencode-support that clear the promotion bars, and for both an executable check beats a prose pattern (bee-capturing: prefer an executable check; escalate a recurring pattern to a durable owner). (1) VERDICT-SHAPE PARITY. The existing three-belt parity test asserts that every blocking RULE reaches every belt, which is why a whole verdict SHAPE could go missing on one runtime and stay green — the defect this feature actually hit, where a host with a narrower return surface honored the one verdict it had a place to put and let the rest go inert. Widen the parity row set from rules to verdict shapes: deny, exit-0 updatedInput repair, exit-0 permissionDecision ask, and unparseable verdict output, asserted per belt. Derive the shapes from the guard's own emit paths (hooks/mod.rs, hooks/write_guard/main.rs, hooks/model_guard.rs), never a hand-authored list — a fourth runtime, or a fifth verdict shape, must fail the suite rather than pass silently. (2) THE SKILLS-VERSION STAMP TRAP. A rendered skills root that exists without its version stamp puts onboarding into blocked_downgrade, which refuses and is never forceable (onboard/skills.rs:420-458) — today the only protection is a comment inside an #[ignore]d regen test, and no test asserts the stamp at all. Add a non-ignored test asserting that every REPO_SKILL_TARGETS root present in this checkout (templates.rs:199-203) carries its version stamp — one test closing the trap for all three roots at once. Do not write a pattern file for either lesson: the tests are the record.

truths: The verdict-shape row set is derived from the guard's emit paths, never hand-authored
A verdict shape missing on one belt fails by name, naming shape and belt
A skills root missing its version stamp fails a non-ignored test, for every present root
No pattern file is authored for either lesson

trace.outcome: Widened the write/model-guard belt-parity test to (rule, verdict-shape) rows and added a non-ignored skills-version-stamp test; both probed to confirm they bite
